correctness.rationale: A complete 126-face independence-complex enumeration and independent 110-face neighborhood enumeration verify their inclusion and all eight elementary free-triangle/tetrahedron pairs, with eight distinct tetrahedra and no other surplus faces. Exact enumeration of the eight-element dihedral automorphism group verifies a single free orbit of pairs, trivial and equal stabilizers, and hence an equivariant collapse. A separate 54-pair acyclic Morse matching reduces the neighborhood complex to one vertex and one two-cell, proving S² integrally. A separate simplicial chain computation verifies all mod-p boundary ranks, exhaustive coloring gives χ=4, and signed fixed-simplex Hopf traces yield the full integral H₂ dihedral character.

originality.rationale: The prior exact same-graph independence-complex calculation already establishes Ind(G)≃S² and the full vertex-deletion dichotomy; these are not new and are explicitly acknowledged. The new statement certifies that the actual inclusion N(G)→Ind(G) is a one-orbit D4-equivariant simplicial collapse, not merely two complexes with abstractly equal homotopy type, and identifies its resulting sharp Lovasz bound and orientation character. This finite relative fact is not implied by the old bare sphere equivalence without additional face/coface verification. Barmak star-cluster theory, Kahle random graph results and Shukla circulant results do not furnish this exact relative collapse. Original 1970 graph-construction full text unavailable; residual priority risk stated.
residual_risks: No absolute priority claim: a calculation of the same neighborhood complex or character may exist in unindexed literature.
The original two-page graph-construction article could not be read in full; public descriptive material was not used to certify noncoverage.

The known Ind(G) sphere type gives substantial prior coverage. Originality and value depend on the *equivariant relative collapse and chromatic interpretation*, not that covered nonequivariant homotopy statement.

value.rationale: The Chvátal graph is the classical smallest triangle-free simultaneously four-regular and four-chromatic graph. A single complete dihedral orbit of elementary collapses connecting its independence complex and Lovasz open-neighborhood complex is a natural, structurally interpretable relationship between two distinct topological constructions; its equivariance and direct inclusion are not supplied by the previously known abstract independence sphere type. The new relative fact proves the Lovasz topological connectivity obstruction is sharp for this extremal graph. The full D4 integral H₂ orientation character is a natural symmetry invariant, not an arbitrary slice. The known chromatic number and Ind sphere are treated as background, not independent gains.
